messages:
lucy: :rotating_light: Root: We are seeing TLS handshake failures for a subset of ingress connections in eu-west-2. Symptoms began ~07:13 UTC. Clients intermittently fail to negotiate SNI and fall back to default cert, causing 502s for some custom-hostname routes. Live status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2073456789

deploy-bot: Auto-detect: sni-mismatch-rate > 5% across 3 ingress clusters. Paging @marc and @infra.

marc: Quick triage: recent automated cert deployment to the edge included a cert bundle where SAN entries were missing wildcard entries for some customer hostnames. Edge routing still accepted connections but handshake selected wrong cert chain when client SNI was absent or truncated.

sara: Impact: Approximately 27 customer routes intermittently returned 502 or TLS handshake errors. Affected customers include a mix of Hosted and Dedicated customers who use custom hostnames. Errors surface for clients with older TLS stacks or aggressive HTTP/2 multiplexing.

infra: Mitigations applied at 07:22 UTC: 1) rolled back to previous cert bundle on eu-west-2 edge gateways, 2) temporarily enabled strict-SNI-enforcement to force correct cert selection where possible, 3) rate-limited deploys to edge cert-service to prevent further rollouts.

lucy: Monitoring: handshake-failure-rate dropped from 6.7% -> 0.3% within 4 minutes after rollback. Canary routes validated. No indication of data corruption; errors are connection-level only.

devops: Hotfix commands (internal ops):

```
# rollback cert bundle on edge nodes (ops only)
EDGE_NODES=$(kubectl get pods -l app=edge-gateway -n edge -o name --selector=region=eu-west-2)
for n in $EDGE_NODES; do
  kubectl exec $n -n edge -- /bin/edge-cert-manager rollback --to=stable-2027-03-01
done
kubectl rollout status deployment/edge-gateway -n edge
```

ops-bot: Scheduled controlled validation window at 08:00 UTC with 2m canary. Please raise objections within 10m.

marc: Customer comms draft: "We experienced an intermittent TLS handshake error affecting custom hostname routes in eu-west-2 due to a certificate bundle deployment. We rolled back the bundle and services have returned to normal. We will follow up with a detailed postmortem and remediation timeline." Ready for send to impacted accounts.

sara: Next actions: 1) regenerate cert bundles ensuring full SAN coverage and run expanded pre-deploy SNI tests, 2) add a preflight that validates client-hello SNI presence across HTTP/2 streams, 3) add alerting on cert-deploy anomaly (SAN delta). Postmortem owners: @marc (deploy/process) and @sara (tests/playbook). ETA for draft: EOD today.

deploy-bot: Severity set to S2 at 07:30 UTC. Monitoring active.

lucy: Thanks team. Please monitor for any regressions and coordinate with #customer-success for follow-up comms. End of broadcast. :white_check_mark:
